title: "Building and Sending Transactions"
description: "Learn how to build, sign, and submit transactions using the Kaptos Kotlin SDK."
sidebar:
  label: "Building Transactions"
---

import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

The Kaptos Kotlin SDK provides namespaced transaction operations via `aptos.transactions`.

<Aside type="note">
All these methods return an `AptosResult<T>`. You can use `when` for pattern matching, or extension functions like `.map()`, `.fold()`, `.getOrNull()`, `.onSuccess()`, and `.onFailure()` to chain operations and handle errors.
</Aside>

## Create Accounts (Setup)

First, let's create our test accounts and client configuration:

```kotlin
val aptos = Aptos(AptosConfig(network = Network.DEVNET))
val alice = Account.generate()
val bob = Account.generate()
aptos.faucet.fund(alice.accountAddress, 100_000_000UL)
```

## Build a Payload

Create an entry function payload describing the on-chain function you want to call. `entryFunctionPayload` fetches the on-chain ABI automatically to encode the arguments into BCS bytes.

```kotlin
val payload = aptos.transactions.entryFunctionPayload(
  function = "0x1::coin::transfer",
  typeArguments = listOf(TypeTag.from("0x1::aptos_coin::AptosCoin")),
  arguments = listOf(
    MoveArgument.from(bob.accountAddress),
    MoveArgument.from(1_000_000UL),
  ),
)
```

## Build the Transaction

Build a raw transaction combining the sender and the payload. 

```kotlin
val txn = aptos.transactions.build(
  sender = alice.accountAddress,
  payload = payload,
)
```

You can optionally specify `TransactionOptions` like the maximum gas amount you're willing to pay.

```kotlin
val txn = aptos.transactions.build(
  sender = alice.accountAddress,
  payload = payload,
  options = TransactionOptions(maxGasAmount = 20_000UL),
)
```

## Sign the Transaction

Sign the transaction to create a sender authenticator.

```kotlin
val auth = aptos.transactions.sign(signer = alice, transaction = txn)
```

## Submit the Transaction

Submit the signed transaction to the network.

```kotlin
val pending = aptos.transactions.submit(
  transaction = txn,
  senderAuthenticator = auth,
)
```

## Wait for Confirmation

Wait for the submitted transaction to be processed.

```kotlin
val confirmed = aptos.transactions.waitForTransaction(pending)
```

## Sign, Submit, and Wait (All-in-one)

You can combine building, signing, submitting, and waiting into a single call:

```kotlin
val confirmed = aptos.transactions.submitAndWait(
  signer = alice,
  payload = payload,
)
```

## Sign and Submit

If you just want to sign and submit without waiting for confirmation:

```kotlin
val pending = aptos.transactions.signAndSubmit(
  signer = alice,
  payload = payload,
)
```

## Multi-Agent Transactions

To build transactions that require multiple signers:

```kotlin
val txn = aptos.transactions.buildMultiAgent(
  sender = alice.accountAddress,
  secondarySigners = listOf(bob.accountAddress),
  payload = payload,
)
```

## Simulate a Transaction

You can simulate a transaction to see its effects without actually executing it on the network.

```kotlin
val simResult = aptos.transactions.simulate(
  transaction = txn,
  senderPublicKey = alice.publicKey,
)
```
